stage_a.note: Very positive, enthusiastic delivery with the mascot adding energetic, highly animated moments.
Pronounced engagement, physical gestures, and loud, clear voices throughout the presentation.
Approachable and friendly orientation, though the delivery is highly scripted and rehearsed.

venture.description: Low-calorie, low-carb, grain-free tortillas and snacks made from fresh-cut jicama.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin introduces himself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa introduces herself, states they are from New York, and asks for the investment amount and equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin brings up the topic of tacos and mentions a doctor's advice against eating them daily.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa attributes the issue to calorie-heavy tortillas and dismisses lettuce wraps as a substitute.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin notes that lettuce wraps break apart easily and lack flavor.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa wishes for a product combining the nutritional benefits of lettuce with the utility of a tortilla.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin introduces their product, JicaWraps, as the solution.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa describes the product as a refreshing tortilla alternative made from fresh jicama slices.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin asks a rhetorical question about the ingredient.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: The mascot yells enthusiastically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin introduces the mascot as a member of a superfood league.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa highlights jicama as their hero ingredient due to its superfood qualities and low calories.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin flexes his muscles energetically.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa adds that the product is super low in carbohydrates.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin flexes again to emphasize the point.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa continues listing benefits, noting it is super high in fiber.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: The mascot flexes and grunts.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa explains the product improves gut health, is perfectly round, pliable, and has a neutral taste.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin lists various dietary lifestyles the product fits, suggesting it as a healthier option for taco nights.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa makes a rhyming remark about replacing traditional tortillas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin makes a pun about doing better with their product.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: The mascot yells enthusiastically again.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin invites the panel to join their movement and enjoy the samples.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark playfully questions the name of the ingredient.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa directs the panel's attention to the samples of tacos, sticks, and pico de gallo provided.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth tastes the provided sample.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin requests a plain wrap without any filling to taste the product itself.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa asks Gwyneth if she has ever tried the root vegetable before.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth confirms it is her first time and describes the pleasant, watery, and slightly sweet taste.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin tastes the plain wrap he requested.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth mentions she included recipes using the ingredient in her recent cookbook.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa expresses pleasant surprise at this information.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks about the manufacturing cost and the retail selling price of the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa provides the production cost, the retail price, and the on-shelf price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks how many individual wraps are included in a single package.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa states the quantity per package and compares the cost per wrap to traditional and grain-free alternatives.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth notes that grain-free products are currently a massive trend in the wellness industry.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara inquires whether the business is currently generating any profits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin details their company history, an early pivot, financial struggles, and significant sales growth over recent years.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth expresses amazement at the sales growth figures.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa provides the specific profit figure for the current year, noting it is similar to the previous year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks where the products are being manufactured.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa explains that processing and sourcing take place in Mexico, where the ingredient is commercially grown.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth asks about the product's shelf life and how long it remains fresh.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa states the shelf life is nineteen days, noting this is significantly longer than typical fresh-cut processors achieve.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks which national retailers or grocery stores currently carry their products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin lists several major retailers and mentions a significant expansion into food service.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks for the total number of store locations they are in.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa answers with the approximate number of doors carrying their product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if that specific store count is responsible for their six million in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin deflects the direct math question by stating the products are very popular.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the requested valuation, arguing that a twenty-five times multiple is unrealistic for their profit level.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa defends the valuation by explaining it is based on a multiple of their projected sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin insists that food businesses have thin margins and reiterates that no one will accept the proposed equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin invites the panel to make offers and expresses willingness to negotiate the equity percentage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara offers the requested funds for ten percent equity, plus a pro-rata share of profits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark states he is not a fan of the ingredient and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Gwyneth explains she prefers to prepare the ingredient herself at home and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori praises the business but decides it is not the right fit for her and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara prompts the founders to respond to her standing offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin counters Barbara's offer by asking if she would accept five percent equity instead.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara rejects the counteroffer and maintains her requirement for ten percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers the requested funds for nine percent equity, including the pro-rata profit distribution.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori clarifies that Kevin's offer also includes the pro-rata profit distribution requirement.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin confirms the pro-rata condition is necessary to recoup his capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin asks the remaining investors if they would be willing to accept seven percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara firmly rejects the seven percent counteroffer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin also rejects the counteroffer, referencing his earlier points about the valuation multiple.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks the founders what kind of help they need from an investor besides capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin explains they have manufacturing handled but need assistance with sales and marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin claims he can provide access to grocery retailers due to his other product lines.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara accuses Kevin of over-promising and asserts her own expertise in sales and marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin makes a joking insult about Barbara, claiming he bought her a broom.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara responds to the joke with a playful threat.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin urges the founders to make a decision between the two standing offers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa counters Barbara's offer with six percent equity plus two percent in advisory shares.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara revises the counteroffer, asking for three percent in advisory shares for a total of nine percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara adds that she is willing to do the deal just to win against Kevin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks the founders what they have decided to do.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Xin accepts Barbara's revised offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara congratulates the founders on securing the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders thank Barbara.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: The mascot yells enthusiastically to celebrate the deal.

decisions.terms: $300,000 for 10% equity and a pro-rata distribution of profits
decisions.note: Wants a share of what they earn.
Great business for them, not the right business for her.

decisions.terms: $300,000 for 9% equity and a pro-rata distribution of profits
decisions.note: Just to make it interesting for Barbara.
Asks if they are willing to do 7%.

decisions.terms: $300,000 for 6% equity and 2% in advisory shares
$300,000 for 6% equity and 3% in advisory shares
decisions.note: Modifies the advisory shares to 3% to total 9%.
